chunks: And by this chain, it was said, Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The debt is a yoke of Allah in His earth. So whenever Allah wants to humiliate a servant, He places it in his neck.

key_terms.رِبْقَةُ: A yoke or halter used to lead an animal, symbolizing burden or subjugation

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and social significance of debt in Shia Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to highlight the spiritual gravity of debt, describing it as a 'yoke' (ribqah) that Allah places upon a servant’s neck as a means of humiliation or testing. This metaphor underscores the psychological and spiritual burden of indebtedness, serving as a practical reminder for believers to settle their dues promptly to avoid divine chastisement or worldly disgrace.
